facts.fact: Cambridge Education's study for the ministry (MEPUA) and UNICEF, from a field mission of 7 to 20 March 2021, finds that pupil lists, enrolment and re-enrolment are managed by hand and separately in each school, that pupils have no unique identifier, and that no system exists to manage enrolment or to follow pupils' schooling and assessments.
facts.system: manual pupil lists kept by each school (no learner-record system)

facts.fact: The same study states that, as found on its mission of March 2021, no system at all exists for managing pupils' enrolment, registration and the follow-up of their schooling and assessments; it gives no count of schools.
facts.system: manual pupil lists kept by each school (no learner-record system)

facts.fact: A roadmap for digitalising the ministry's administrative and teaching management was validated by MEPUA, ANIEN and UNICEF on 2 November 2021; it provides for a single integrated information and management system whose pupil module covers attendance and absence, class assessments, transfers and examination results, with a unique pupil number and an electronic file per pupil.
facts.system: système d'information et de gestion unique et intégré (SIGE, planned)

note: The file ends mid-sentence in section 3.3.2 (line 642): sections 4 and 5 of the report are not in the capture. Read whole, in two reads. 'Schools: none' rests on the report's flat statement that no system exists; the same report lists a secondary pupil-registration initiative and the AGEST tablet application without saying what either records, so both are unclassified. Other statements: the school statistics run on Access and Excel throughout; apart from the annual statistical collections no system manages schools day to day; only 3 deconcentrated offices, 4% of IRE/DPE, reported an office internet connection; Kobotoolbox was proposed by respondents for the census, not adopted.
